long_biography.plain_text:
Shipping was the inherited platform rather than a venture Kassidokostas-Latsis founded. His grandfather established the business in the 1940s, and he later assumed enhanced responsibilities at Latsco. He directed a newbuilding programme focused on product tankers and gas carriers, later adding very large crude carriers and the family's first LNG ships. He also formed separate partnerships for second-hand bulk carriers and tankers.

His entertainment work followed a different path. After studying in London and spending time in Los Angeles, he helped create 1821 Media. In 2015 he initiated the Hercules Film Fund, bringing European institutional and family-office capital into independent productions in the United States and Europe. That vehicle has financed more than 25 films, while his producer credits have continued alongside his shipping leadership.

Latsco's board report uses Christian Paris Kassidokostas, while public business sources use Paris Kassidokostas-Latsis and spelling variants with one or two s characters. The corporate form does not establish whether Christian belongs in the website's middle-name field, so no name-field addition is proposed.
Lower-authority film databases give Athens, but the reviewed primary and established business sources only establish that he spent most of his childhood in Greece. Place of birth remains blank.

Latsco is a privately owned multigenerational family company. Sources establish Kassidokostas-Latsis's leadership and operating contribution but do not disclose his exact personal share. The dossier therefore does not attribute the entire fleet, wider Latsis holdings or company value solely to him.

1821 Media, Hercules Film Fund and the Marla or Ivy maritime vehicles have direct founder, supervisor or ownership evidence. No equivalently strong public evidence was found for a separate technology-investment platform, so none is attributed.
